title: Polynomial augmentations: standard resolution and boundary lifting criterion
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $Q_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$ be an augmented simplicial $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For a simplicial abelian group $M$ put $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$ for $n\geq0$, with differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ for $n>0$, and zero positive terms. The constant augmentation $s(\operatorname{const}B)\to B[0]$, identity in degree zero and zero in negative degrees, is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If every $Q_n\to B$ is surjective and $s(Q_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $Q_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$ is a trivial Kan fibration [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], including the boundary lifting condition in dimension zero. Let $F_A(E)=A[E]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $U$ forget $A$-algebras to sets, put $G=F_AU$, and let $\epsilon:G\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\delta=F_A\eta U:G\to G^2$ be evaluation and the map induced by the adjunction unit. The terms $P_n=G^{n+1}B$, with faces $G^i\epsilon G^{n-i}$, degeneracies $G^i\delta G^{n-i}$ and the iterated evaluation augmentation, form an augmented simplicial $A$-algebra. Every $P_n$ is polynomial and every $P_n\to B$ is surjective. The underlying simplicial-set augmentation is a homotopy equivalence (a homotopy inverse and homotopies are maps of simplicial sets, without any additivity requirement). Its additive alternating augmentation $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism and its underlying simplicial-set augmentation is a trivial Kan fibration. No finiteness assumption on the rings or sets of polynomial variables is imposed.

proof.text: For the constant simplicial abelian group $B$, every face is the identity. Hence the differential from degree $-n$ is zero for odd $n$ and the identity for even $n>0$. Its degree-zero cohomology is $B/0=B$. In degree $-n<0$, if $n$ is even its kernel is zero, and if $n$ is odd the incoming differential from degree $-(n+1)$ is the identity, so the cohomology is zero. Positive terms vanish. The stated augmentation is a chain map and induces the identity on $H^0$ and isomorphisms between zero groups elsewhere; it is therefore a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $q:Q_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$ for the augmentation. Its additive alternating map satisfies $s(Q)\xrightarrow{s(q)}s(\operatorname{const}B)\to B[0]$ equal to the augmentation assumed in the statement. For every $r$, the second map on $H^r$ is invertible by Step 1 and the composite is invertible by hypothesis, so $H^r(s(q))$ is invertible. Every $q_n$ is surjective by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-surjective-quasi-iso-boundary-lifting] to the additive simplicial groups underlying $Q$ and $\operatorname{const}B$. It gives the required boundary fillers in every dimension. In dimension zero the boundary is empty and the required lift is precisely a preimage under $Q_0\to B$.

proof.text: The polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] identifies functions $E\to UC$ with $A$-algebra maps $A[E]\to C$, naturally in $E$ and $C$. Thus $F_A\dashv U$, with unit $e\mapsto x_e$ and counit evaluation $x_c\mapsto c$. The first triangle identity holds on each generator $x_e$ and on coefficients; the second sends each $c$ to $x_c$ and back to $c$. Apply [lem-trf-adjunction-standard-simplicial-homotopy] to this adjunction and $a=B$. Its formulas are exactly $P_n=G^{n+1}B$, the faces and degeneracies in the statement, and the iterated evaluation augmentation. It gives both the augmented simplicial algebra and a homotopy equivalence of its underlying simplicial sets. The homotopy inverse and homotopies live in sets; no additivity of those maps is used.

proof.text: Each $P_n=F_A(UG^nB)=A[UG^nB]$ is polynomial. Write $a_n:G^{n+1}B\to B$ for its augmentation and put $t_{-1}(b)=b$, $t_n(b)=x_{t_{n-1}(b)}\in G^{n+1}B$. Evaluation gives $a_0(t_0(b))=b$; recursively $a_n(t_n(b))=a_{n-1}(t_{n-1}(b))=b$. These set-theoretic preimages prove surjectivity for all $n\geq0$. The polynomial universal property permits arbitrary sets of variables, so this argument imposes no finiteness condition.

proof.text: The augmentation $p:P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$ is additive because its components are algebra maps. Its underlying simplicial-set map is a homotopy equivalence by Step 3. Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-set-homotopy-quasi-iso] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $s(p):s(P)\to s(\operatorname{const}B)$, although the chosen inverse and homotopies need not be additive. Composing with the constant augmentation of Step 1 gives the required quasi-isomorphism $s(P)\to B[0]$: its cohomology maps are composites of isomorphisms. Step 4 supplies degreewise surjectivity, so the criterion proved in Step 2 now gives the trivial Kan fibration, including dimension zero.

The statement is unchanged apart from one added citation: [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] in the text and in stmt_deps. The item is still unsplit in clones/live and clones/side-live, and it has no repair note. Sources read: cotangent.tex 08PM, 08PT (first proof) and 08QI; simplicial.tex 08ND, 08P2, 08P1 and 0197; tags checked against stacks-project/tags/tags; no SGA. The proof is the 08PT first proof plus the 08QI criterion. Step 1: the alternating differential of s(const B) is 0 for odd n and the identity for even n>0, so H^0=B and all other cohomology is 0; this is elementary. Step 2: s(Q)->s(const B)->B[0] composes to q_0; 2-out-of-3 makes s(q) a quasi-isomorphism; lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-surjective-quasi-iso-boundary-lifting then gives fillers for all n>=0, and n=0 is the p_0 surjectivity clause of def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration. Step 3: the polynomial universal property gives the adjunction F_A ⊣ U (triangle identities checked on generators); lem-trf-adjunction-standard-simplicial-homotopy with a=B gives exactly the item's terms, faces, degeneracies and augmentation, and the homotopy equivalence on underlying sets (08ND). Step 4: t_n(b)=x_{t_{n-1}(b)} and a_n=a_{n-1}∘d_0 with d_0=ε_{G^nB}, which gives surjectivity in every degree for arbitrary variable sets. Step 5: lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-set-homotopy-quasi-iso does not require an additive inverse or homotopies (08P2); composing with Step 1 and applying Step 2 gives the trivial Kan fibration. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, there is no cycle, and all three cited lemmas are reviewed and in sk-i-curve-zero, so no tool_uses are needed. Edge cases checked: B=0, the identity A->A, infinite rings and variable sets, characteristic 2. Duplicates: def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data, lem-trf-polynomial-resolution-extension-trivial-kan, lem-trf-constant-polynomial-resolution-retraction and the cotangent citers do not state the item. Route pivot: def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration is the classical combinatorial notion (Stacks 08NL, Mathlib match SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.I.rlp), used only for the 08QI/08P1 resolution criterion; it was already in the base statement and its use is justified at Steps 2 and 5. 'Simplicial set' means the ordinary underlying simplicial set and involves no enhancement machinery. Both are accepted.

lean.statement: theorem polynomial_augmentation_boundary (f : Arrow CommRingCat.{u}) : QuasiIso (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex.ε.app (⟨(SimplicialObject.const AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj ((forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat ⋙ forget₂ RingCat AddCommGrpCat).obj f.right), (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat ⋙ forget₂ RingCat AddCommGrpCat).obj f.right, 𝟙 _⟩)) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat) ∧ (∀ Q : Augmentation f, (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (Q.augmentation.app (op ⦋n⦌))) → QuasiIso (additiveAugmentation Q) → SSet.Enhanced.trivialKanFibration (Functor.whiskerRight Q.augmentation (forget CommRingCat.{u}))) ∧ ∃ P : Augmentation f, IsStandard P ∧ IsPolynomialResolution P ∧ (∃ g : (SimplicialObject.const CommRingCat.{u}).obj f.right ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u} ⟶ P.algebra ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}, Relation.EqvGen (fun a b ↦ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy a b)) (Functor.whiskerRight P.augmentation (forget CommRingCat.{u}) ≫ g) (𝟙 (P.algebra ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u})) ∧ Relation.EqvGen (fun a b ↦ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy a b)) (g ≫ Functor.whiskerRight P.augmentation (forget CommRingCat.{u})) (𝟙 ((SimplicialObject.const CommRingCat.{u}).obj f.right ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))) ∧ SSet.Enhanced.trivialKanFibration (Functor.whiskerRight P.augmentation (forget CommRingCat.{u}))
